rule: Lay out both nc_matmul operands with the contraction dimension (K) on the partition axis; deliver the LHS pre-transposed ([K, M]) from HBM.
why: The PE array contracts over the 128 partitions of both stationary and moving tiles; a [M,K] LHS would need an on-chip transpose per tile.
trigger: Any matmul; HBM tensors whose contraction dim is the inner (free) dim.
fix: Store weights as [K, N] / activations as [K, M] in HBM (or dma_transpose on load); nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=lhsT_tile[K,M], moving=rhs_tile[K,N]).
check_sketch: flag nc_matmul whose stationary/moving partition dim != shared contraction dim

rule: Give the stationary operand at most 128 free columns and the moving operand at most 512 free columns per nc_matmul.
why: gemm_stationary_fmax=128 and gemm_moving_fmax=512 are the PE/PSUM-bank limits; the moving free dim maps directly onto one 2KB PSUM bank (512 fp32).
trigger: Choosing which operand is stationary; tile sizes.
fix: TILE_M = nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax (128); TILE_N = nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax (512); loop M in 128s and N in 512s.
check_sketch: stationary.shape[1] <= 128 and moving.shape[1] <= 512

rule: For token-generation (small T) projections, make the WEIGHT tile [128(H0), 128(I0)] the stationary operand and the hidden tile [128(H0), T] the moving operand, producing output with I on the partition axis ([I0, I/128, T]).
why: With T<=128 the hidden tile would under-fill the 512-wide moving slot; swapping lets each matmul consume a full 128x128 weight tile and the result [I0, T] lands with the next layer's contraction dim (I) already on partitions, so no transpose is needed before down_proj.
trigger: batch*seqlen small (nkilib: BxS <= 96 selects TKG); this is the default MLP TKG mode (use_tkg_*_column_tiling=False).
fix: for h1: for i_tile in TiledRange(I,128): nisa.nc_matmul(psum[i][0:128,0:T], weight_sb[:, h1, i_tile] , hidden_sb[:, h1_slice_T])  # output [I, T]
check_sketch: if T <= 128 and nc_matmul(stationary=activation[:,T]) then suggest swap

rule: When keeping hidden as the stationary operand with T<128, pack column_tiling_factor=128//column_tiling_dim independent H1 tiles side-by-side in the PE array via tile_position/tile_size and sum the PSUM column bands afterward.
why: A [128, T=32] stationary tile leaves columns 32..127 of the PE array idle; column tiling runs up to 4 partial products in parallel (up to 4x PE throughput) at the cost of a few tensor_tensor adds to fold the bands.
fix: col_dim = 32 if T<=32 else 64 if T<=64 else 128 (gen2: 64); nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum[nl.ds(col_dim*c, T), :], stationary=hidden[:, h1], moving=w[:, h1, :512], tile_position=(0, col_dim*c), tile_size=(128, col_dim)); then tensor_tensor add bands.
check_sketch: T < 128 and nc_matmul without tile_position on activation-stationary path

rule: On NeuronCore-v2 (trn1) do not use tile_size with both row and column equal to 32; use column_tiling_dim=64.
why: Hardware restriction on gen2 PE sub-tiling.
trigger: nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen2 and column tiling with T<=32.
fix: if nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen2: column_tiling_dim = 64
check_sketch: tile_size==(32,32) and target gen2

rule: Bound the number of output columns produced per inner loop by (8 PSUM banks) x (per-bank width): 128*8=1024 when weights are stationary, 512*8=4096 when hidden is stationary; shard I in those chunks.
why: Each PSUM bank holds one 128x512 fp32 accumulator; a loop that needs more than 8 live accumulators must spill/reload PSUM.
trigger: I (intermediate) > 1024 in swap mode or > 4096 in column-tiling mode.
fix: max_I_shard_size = _pmax*8 (swap) or _psum_fmax*8 (column); for i_tile in TiledRange(I, max_I_shard_size): ...
check_sketch: count live PSUM accumulators per loop > 8

rule: In LHS/RHS-swap down_proj, pack perBankT = 512//T consecutive H1 output tiles ([128, T] each) into one PSUM bank along the free axis; if ceil(H1_shard/perBankT) > 8 banks, fall back to CTE mode.
why: Each [128,T] result uses only T of the 512 columns; packing keeps all H1_shard accumulators live in PSUM so the I-contraction can be fully accumulated without eviction.
trigger: down_proj with small T; H large.
fix: perBankT = psum_fmax // T; psum_idx = h1 // perBankT; nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psums[psum_idx][0:128, nl.ds((h1 % perBankT)*T, T)], stationary=w_tile, moving=hidden_tile)
check_sketch: kernel_assert(div_ceil(H1_shard, 512//T) <= 8)

rule: Pre-permute down_proj weights offline so each [128(I0), 128(H0)] stationary tile is contiguous in SBUF; otherwise the kernel must read the weight tile with stride H1_shard via reshape_dim+permute.
why: A strided stationary read costs PE/SBUF bandwidth on every matmul; permuting once in the framework removes the stride.
trigger: use_tkg_down_proj_optimized_layout flag; weight access shows reshape_dim(...).permute(...) in the hot loop.
fix: weight_reshaped = w_tile.reshape_dim(dim=1, shape=(H0, num_Htiles)).permute((0,2,1)) -> replace by offline permute + plain slice(dim=1, h1*128, (h1+1)*128)
check_sketch: permute() applied to a stationary operand inside matmul loop

rule: Load MLP weights in large [HTile, I] slabs (HTile=2048 bf16 / 4096 quantized, min 512) into a ring of up to 4 SBUF weight tiles shared by gate and up projections.
why: Fewer, larger DMAs saturate HBM bandwidth for the memory-bound decode MLP; a ring of >=2 tiles lets the next slab load while the current one is consumed.
trigger: Weight loads of [128, I] granularity or single-buffered weight tiles.
fix: HTile=min(H_per_shard, 2048); w_tile = sbm.alloc_stack((128, HTile//128, I_shard)); weight_idx=(base+h_tile.index)%num_allocated; while num_available<4 and HTile>=512: HTile//=2
check_sketch: weight dma_copy per 128-row tile inside matmul loop

rule: When a second projection (up, then down) reuses the gate weight ring buffer, start its tile index at (num_required_tiles % num_allocated) so it writes the slot least recently read.
why: Writing into the slot the previous projection just read creates a WAR anti-dependency that serializes the DMA behind the matmul; offsetting lets the next weights stream in early.
trigger: Two phases share SBUF weight buffers.
fix: weight_base_idx = div_ceil(H, HTile) % num_allocated_w_tile if is_up_proj else 0; for down: if 0 < overlapped_addr < n*size: weight_base_idx = div_ceil(overlap, size)
check_sketch: ring buffer reused across phases with base index 0

rule: Select the token-generation (TKG) kernel variants when batch*seqlen <= 96; otherwise use the context-encoding (CTE) variants.
why: Below ~96 tokens the projection is HBM-bound on weights, so weight-stationary/column-tiled layouts win; above that the PE is better fed with activations stationary.
fix: is_tkg = mode in (AUTO, DECODE) and B*S <= 96 and not force_cte_mode
check_sketch: B*S <= 96 -> tkg

rule: Tile the token axis of the TKG MLP in BS_TILE_SIZE=128 chunks and T-shard across LNC cores only when T >= 128*lnc and T % lnc == 0; otherwise shard on H.
why: A 128-token tile fills the partition dim for the output transpose and one PSUM column band; small T is better split along H so both cores stream half the weights.
fix: use_t_sharding = T >= 128*lnc and lnc>=2 and T%lnc==0; else H-shard with sendrecv of partial sums

rule: Under LNC=2 shard gate/up/down weights along H (each core computes a partial contraction), then exchange fp32 partials with nisa.sendrecv and add; apply bias on shard 0 only.
why: Each core only reads half the weights (the bandwidth bottleneck); the exchange of a [T, I] fp32 tile is cheap relative to the weights saved. Adding bias on both cores would double-count it.
fix: nisa.sendrecv(src=gate_up_fp32, dst=recv, send_to_rank=1-shard_id, recv_from_rank=1-shard_id, pipe_id=0); nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=gate_up_fp32, data1=gate_up_fp32, data2=recv, op=nl.add); is_bias = bias is not None and shard_id == 0
check_sketch: bias add present on all shards when H-sharded

rule: Allocate gate and up fp32 outputs contiguously ([T, 2*I]) so a single sendrecv exchanges both partials.
why: One larger DMA has lower fixed overhead than two and halves the cross-core synchronisation points.
trigger: LNC>1 and both gate and up are computed.
fix: gate_up_sb_fp32 = sbm.alloc_stack((T, 2*I), fp32); gate_view = [:, :I]; up_view = [:, I:]; one nisa.sendrecv on the whole buffer
check_sketch: two consecutive sendrecv on adjacent buffers

rule: Use dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma for LNC sendrecv when the per-partition free size is <= 256 elements (<=1024 bytes); otherwise use the regular DMA.
why: gpsimd_dma routes SBUF-to-SBUF without bouncing through HBM, eliminating PSEUDO_CORE_BARRIER stalls, but has a 256-element/partition hardware limit.
trigger: Exchanging rmsnorm partial sums, softmax max/sum stats, small partials.
fix: if free_elems <= 256: nisa.sendrecv(..., dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma) else nisa.sendrecv(...)
check_sketch: sendrecv with small src and no dma_engine

rule: Pad partition counts to a multiple of 16 for tensors fed to GPSIMD extended instructions (gpsimd sb2sb sendrecv).
why: Extended ISA requires input/output tensors to span whole 16-partition GPSIMD cores.
fix: padded = (p + 15)//16*16; buf = sbm.alloc_stack((padded, n), ...)
check_sketch: gpsimd sendrecv src.shape[0] % 16 != 0

rule: For RMSNorm with T >= 128 tokens use the [T(partition), H(free)] layout with one fused activation_reduce(square, add) per tile; for T < 128 (decode) use [H0, T, H1] with a ones-matrix matmul to finish the reduction across partitions.
why: A free-axis reduction is one ScalarE instruction, but it needs tokens on partitions; in decode only a handful of tokens exist, so H is spread over partitions and the cross-partition sum is done on the PE with ones[128,128] @ sq[128,T].
trigger: Any pre-norm in a decode megakernel.
fix: nisa.activation(sq, op=nl.square, data=x[128,T,H1]); nisa.tensor_reduce(red, nl.add, sq, axis=2); nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=ones[128,128], moving=red[128,T]); nisa.activation(red, op=nl.rsqrt, data=psum, scale=1/H, bias=eps_sb)
check_sketch: rmsnorm with T<128 using free-axis-only reduction

rule: Compute 1/sqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) as a single ScalarE activation: op=rsqrt, scale=1/H, bias=eps tensor.
why: activation computes f(scale*x + bias); folding mean and epsilon avoids two extra vector ops and keeps the reduction in fp32.
fix: nisa.activation(dst=inv, op=nl.rsqrt, data=sumsq, scale=hidden_scale, bias=eps_sb)

rule: Shard RMSNorm on H across LNC cores (exchanging the [T,1] sum-of-squares via sendrecv) only when T >= 18 and H1 % lnc == 0; for smaller T each core redundantly normalizes the full row.
why: Below ~18 tokens the sendrecv round-trip costs more than the halved compute; the threshold was tuned empirically.
fix: shard_on_h = (H1 % lnc == 0) and (18 <= T)

rule: Issue work that is independent of the cross-core exchange (e.g. x*gamma) before the sendrecv so it overlaps the communication latency.
why: sendrecv blocks on the other core; moving the gamma multiply ahead fills that idle time.
trigger: Any kernel with sendrecv in the critical path.
fix:
nisa.tensor_tensor(gamma_mult, x_shard, gamma_bcast, nl.multiply)  # before sendrecv
nisa.sendrecv(...); add; rsqrt; final multiply

rule: When transposing [T, H] norm output into [H0, H2, T], pack tiles_per_psum = 512 // padded_T transposes into one PSUM bank and drain it with one tensor_tensor that also multiplies by gamma.
why: Fewer, larger PSUM evictions reduce per-instruction overhead and the gamma multiply rides for free on the eviction.
fix: padded_T = ((T*2+3)//4)*4//2; per = 512//padded_T; tp_psum=(128, per*padded_T); for i: nisa.nc_transpose(tp_psum[:, i*padded_T : i*padded_T+T], src_i); nisa.tensor_tensor(dst, tp_psum_view, gamma_bcast, nl.multiply)
check_sketch: nc_transpose followed by per-tile tensor_copy

rule: For H_per_shard <= 2048, load the [T, H] activation contiguously and transpose on-chip (nc_transpose) instead of a strided dma_copy that scatters H across partitions.
why: A strided HBM read with 128 partition-strided streams of short runs under-utilises DMA; one contiguous DMA plus PE transposes is faster for small H.
trigger: Decode input load of hidden [T,H] into [H0, T, H1].
fix: if H_per_shard <= _CONTIGUOUS_LOAD_H_THRESHOLD: dma_copy(tmp[T,H]); for h1: nc_transpose(psum, tmp[:, h1*128:(h1+1)*128]); tensor_copy(out[:, :, h1], psum) else: dma_copy(dst=out, src=x.reshape_dim(1,[nshard,128,H1]).permute([2,0,1,3]).select(2,shard), dge_mode=3)
check_sketch: strided dma_copy with partition stride on H when H <= 2048

rule: Store RoPE channels in contiguous [first_half | second_half] order on the partition axis so rotate-half is two partition-sliced tensor_tensor ops; convert interleaved [even,odd,...] layouts with stride-2 DMA slices, or a permutation matmul only when B*heads*S <= 512.
why: Contiguous halves let x[:half] and x[half:] be addressed as partition ranges; interleaved layouts need a gather. The matmul relayout is limited by gemm_moving_fmax.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=x_sb[:half], src=x.slice(0,0,d,2)); nisa.dma_copy(dst=x_sb[half:], src=x.slice(0,1,d,2))  # interleaved->contiguous on load
check_sketch: RoPE on interleaved layout with B*heads*S > 512 using matmul relayout

rule: Copy the upper half of a partition-split tensor into a separate buffer starting at partition 0 before using it in tensor_tensor with the lower half.
why: tensor_tensor requires its operands' base partitions to be aligned (same quadrant offset); x[half_d:] starts at partition 32/64, x[:half_d] at 0.
trigger: rotate-half RoPE, any op mixing partition slices at different offsets.
fix: sb_odd = nl.ndarray((half_d, ...)); nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sb_odd, src=x_in_sb[half_d:]); nisa.tensor_tensor(out, x_in_sb[:half_d], sb_odd, ...)
check_sketch: tensor_tensor operands with different partition start offsets

rule: Size RoPE batch/head groups so 7 full [d, b, h, S] buffers + 2 cos/sin buffers fit sbuf_fmax_bytes per partition; the allocator cannot spill.
why: LinearScanAllocation has no spill path; exceeding per-partition SBUF is a compile failure (B*n_heads*S <= ~73728 bf16).
fix: tile_cost = 7*tile*dtype_bytes; cossin = 2*tile*dtype_bytes; batch_group = max(1, min(B, budget // (tile_cost*n_heads + cossin)))
check_sketch: sum of live SBUF bytes per partition > nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes

rule: Implement rotate-half as a single nc_matmul against a signed block-circulant permutation matrix built from the shared identity when the Vector/Scalar engines are the bottleneck.
why: The PE is often idle in decode; a [128,128] stationary rotation matrix performs the shift and negation in one instruction. nc_matmul applies stationary.T, so build the inverse shift.
trigger: Fused RoPE inside attention/QKV where DVE/ACT are saturated.
fix: rot = build_rotation_matrix(128, 1, shifts=64, dtype=nl.float16, negate=True); nisa.nc_matmul(psum, stationary=rot, moving=x)

rule: Reduce angle arguments to [-pi, pi] (modulo) before calling the sine activation on ScalarE.
why: The ACT engine sine is only accurate inside [-pi, pi].
trigger: In-kernel cos/sin generation for RoPE from position ids.
fix: emb = emb - 2*pi*floor((emb+pi)/(2*pi)); nisa.activation(dst, op=nl.sin, data=emb)
check_sketch: nl.sin activation without preceding range reduction

rule: In token-generation attention compute scores as K^T-stationary: stationary=K tile [d, 128 kv positions], moving=Q [d, bs*q_head*s_active], giving a transposed score tile [128 kv, bqs] with kv positions on partitions.
why: The kv axis then sits on partitions for the PV matmul contraction with no transpose of the (large) K/V; only the small exp tile needs transposing. 4K-position groups keep PSUM < 512 columns.
fix: mm1_grp_sz = 4096; if (mm1_grp_sz//128)*s_active_qh > 512: mm1_grp_sz = (512//s_active_qh)*128; nisa.nc_matmul(qk_psum[:, j*s_qh:(j+1)*s_qh], stationary=k_sb[:, j*128:(j+1)*128], moving=q_sb)

rule: Compute the PV product as V^T-stationary: nc_matmul(stationary=V tile [128 kv, d], moving=exp^T [128 kv, bqs]) which yields (exp @ V)^T = [d, bqs] with d_head on partitions.
why: Keeps the output in [d, B*heads*S] layout that the following o_proj consumes with d on the contraction/partition axis; no final transpose.
fix: nisa.nc_matmul(exp_v_psum[0:d, 0:s_qh], stationary=v_sb[:, t*d:(t+1)*d], moving=exp_t[:, t, b*s_qh:(b+1)*s_qh])  # accumulate over t

rule: When d_head < 128 (and d_head % 32 == 0) pack 128//d_head consecutive kv tiles into one nc_matmul (dense) or into partition bands via tile_position (col), then fold the bands; enable only for s_prior >= 8192 and block-KV layouts.
why: A 64-wide V stationary tile wastes half the PE rows; packing two tiles doubles PE utilisation. Dense packing is preferred (fewer instructions) when factor*s_active_qh <= 512.
fix: factor = 128//d_head; nisa.nc_matmul(psum[:factor*d, :factor*s_qh], stationary=v_sb[:, t*d:(t+factor)*d], moving=exp_view)  # valid blocks on the diagonal
check_sketch: nc_matmul stationary partition dim < 128 with s_prior >= 8192

rule: For d_head=64 with block KV, pack two kv positions per 128-partition column (row tiling) and replicate Q into both partition halves with cross_partition_copy so one matmul covers 256 kv positions.
why: Fills the unused 64 partitions of the contraction axis; requires Q duplicated across halves and separate PSUM banks per row-tile half.
fix: qk_row_tile_factor = 2 if (auto_alloc and d_head==64 and use_dma_transpose and block_len>=2) else 1; _replicate_q_for_row_tiling via cross_partition_copy (nc_stream_shuffle)

rule: Produce the row max already negated (tensor_reduce(..., negate=True) or multiply by -1) and pass it as the bias of the exp activation, fusing max-subtraction, exp and the row-sum into one ScalarE instruction.
why: nisa.activation computes exp(scale*x + bias) with an optional accumulate reduce; feeding -max as bias removes the separate subtract pass and the separate sum pass, and frees the Vector engine.
trigger: Any softmax (prefill or decode) on gen2/gen3.
fix: nisa.tensor_reduce(dst=row_max, op=nl.maximum, data=qk, axis=(1,), negate=True); nisa.activation(dst=exp_row, op=nl.exp, data=qk_psum, bias=row_max, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=sum_tile, reduce_cmd=nisa.reduce_cmd.reset_reduce)
check_sketch: tensor_scalar(subtract max) followed by activation(exp) followed by tensor_reduce(add)

rule: On trn3 (gen4 sub-version 1) use nisa.exponential (Vector engine, subtracts max_value directly) for softmax exp and move the PSUM eviction to the Scalar engine; on earlier generations use nisa.activation(exp) on ScalarE and evict on VectorE.
why: Keeps the exp and the transpose-eviction on different engines so they overlap.
trigger: Softmax in a decode kernel targeting multiple generations.
fix: if is_trn3_b1(): nisa.exponential(dst, src, max_value=max, reduce_res=sum, reduce_cmd=...); evict_engine=nisa.scalar_engine else: nisa.activation(..., bias=neg_max, ...); evict_engine=nisa.vector_engine

rule: Issue softmax exp in chunks of ~1024 free elements (8 x 128 kv tiles) rather than one instruction over the whole row.
why: Balances per-instruction overhead against letting the downstream 128-wide PE transposes start earlier (pipelining).
fix: exp_grp_size = 8; for g in range(div_ceil(n_sprior_tiles, 8)): nisa.activation(dst[:, g*1024:(g+1)*1024], op=nl.exp, ..., reduce_cmd=reset_reduce if g==0 else reduce)

rule: Group 512//bsq transposes of [bsq, 128] exp chunks into one wide PSUM bank and evict the whole bank with a single strided tensor_copy.
why: Fewer, larger PSUM->SBUF copies cut per-instruction overhead on the eviction engine.
trigger: Transposing softmax probabilities for PV; any batch of small transposes.
fix: tp_grp = max(1, 512 // bsq); tp_psum = nl.ndarray((128, grp_n*bsq)); for j: nisa.nc_transpose(tp_psum3d[:, j, :], exp[:bsq, j*128:(j+1)*128]); nisa.tensor_copy(dst_view_strided, tp_psum3d, engine=...)
check_sketch: nc_transpose each followed by its own tensor_copy

rule: For s_prior > 256 on gen4, split the strided max-reduce between VectorE (tensor_reduce on first half of rows) and ScalarE (activate2 with reduce_op=max on the second half); for small S do it in one tensor_reduce.
why: Parallelises the reduction across two engines; for tiny inputs the split overhead exceeds the gain and activate2 is gen4-only.
fix: if s_prior > 256 and gen4: tensor_reduce(first_half); for i: nisa.activate2(dst=view_i, op=nl.copy, data=view_i, imm0=1.0, imm1=0.0, op0=nl.multiply, op1=nl.add, reduce_op=nl.max, reduce_res=qk_max[:, i], reduce_cmd=reset_reduce)

rule: Carry online-softmax state (m, l, acc) across KV tiles with nl.sequential_range (not affine_range), initialise m to -inf, and rebase with exp(m_old - m_new) which is 0 on the first tile.
why: The dependency between tiles is real; affine_range would let the compiler reorder. The -inf init makes the first rebase wipe the empty state without a special case.
fix: m = nl.full((g,1), -inf); for t in nl.sequential_range(n): new_m = max(m, tile_max); r = exp(m-new_m); l = l*r + tile_l; acc = acc*r + pv; m[...] = new_m
check_sketch: affine_range loop writes and reads same SBUF state

rule: Multiply by 1/sum once on the [128, d_head] attention output instead of normalising every [128, seqlen_kv] probability tile.
why: Moves O(seqlen_kv) multiplies to O(d_head); softmax(x)@V == (exp(x)@V)/sum.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=attn_out, data=attn_out_psum, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=inverse_sum_row)  # after PV accumulation
check_sketch: tensor_scalar(multiply by 1/sum) applied to exp tile before PV matmul

rule: Write the exp output in bf16 (let the ScalarE activation cast) before nc_transpose and PV; keep max/sum in fp32.
why: PE transposes and matmuls run faster on 2-byte data and ScalarE casts for free; the fp32 statistics preserve accuracy.
fix: exp_row = nl.ndarray((128, kv), dtype=nl.bfloat16); nisa.activation(dst=exp_row, op=nl.exp, data=qk_psum, bias=neg_max, reduce_res=sum_fp32)
check_sketch: nc_transpose on fp32 tile that was produced by activation

rule: Keep QK^T scores and running max/sum in fp32 (inter_type) while I/O stays bf16; projection intermediates (gate/up) are also fp32 in SBUF.
why: nc_matmul accumulates in fp32 anyway; keeping the softmax statistics in fp32 avoids bf16 cancellation in max-subtraction and partial-sum exchanges across cores.
fix: qk_sbuf = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype=nl.float32); gate_sb = sbm.alloc_stack(shape, dtype=nl.float32, align=4)
check_sketch: softmax statistics buffers in bf16

rule: Under LNC=2 shard attention on batch when bs % 2 == 0 and (bs*q_head*s_active >= 128 or curr_sprior <= 256); otherwise shard s_prior (requires curr_sprior >= 256) and merge partial softmax stats via sendrecv.
why: Batch sharding keeps both cores running identical code with one partition tile each; s_prior sharding is needed for batch=1 long context and costs a cross-core max/sum exchange and output add.
trigger: Decode attention with batch=1 -> s_prior sharded.
fix: batch_sharded = bs%2==0 and (bs*q_head*s_active >= 128 or curr_sprior <= 2*128); sprior_sharded = not batch_sharded and curr_sprior >= 2*128

rule: When s_prior is sharded for block KV, assign flash-attention tiles to cores alternately (NC0 even tiles, NC1 odd) instead of contiguous halves.
why: With DMA skipping of inactive blocks a partially filled cache would leave one core idle; interleaving balances work.
fix: nc_start_offset = prg_id * tile_size; tile stride = 2 * tile_size

rule: Tile s_prior in 8192-position flash-attention tiles (only when s_prior > 8192) and tile the batch so 8*bs*q_head*s_active*fa_tile <= 16 MiB (10 bytes/elem for fp32 I/O).
why: The qk fp32 tile, its bf16 exp copy and the mask must stay comfortably inside SBUF.
fix: use_fa = s_prior > 8192; per_batch = (10 if fp32 else 8)*q_head*s_active*fa_tile; max_bs = 16MiB // per_batch

rule: Interleave at most min(bs, 8) batches across PSUM banks and give each batch 8 // degree banks for its inner multi-buffering; reduce the degree further if SBUF cannot hold that many batch working sets.
why: There are 8 PSUM banks; splitting them between cross-batch and intra-batch pipelining is the only way to keep PE busy while ScalarE/VectorE evict.
fix: batch_interleave = min(bs, 8); safe = min(batch_interleave, free_sbuf // per_batch_bytes); per_batch_interleave = 8 // safe; psum address = (i % safe) * 2048

rule: Load block KV K tiles with indirect nisa.dma_transpose (uint32 block indices) when elements are 2 bytes (bf16/fp16 or fp8 packed pairwise into bf16) and block_len >= 8; otherwise gather with indirect dma_copy and transpose on the PE.
why: dma_transpose only supports 2-byte elements; for tiny blocks or few batches its setup overhead exceeds the PE path. The DMA path frees the TensorE for matmul.
trigger: Paged KV cache K load in decode.
fix: if not fp8_packed and (block_len < 8 or (block_len <= 16 and d_head <= 16 and bs < 4 and n_prgs == 2)): use_dma_transpose = False

rule: Store fp8 K cache as [num_blocks, block_len//2, d_head, 2] so pairs of positions form 2-byte units that dma_transpose can move; nc_transpose does not support fp8 at all (cast to bf16 first).
why: DMA transpose requires 2-byte elements; the PE transpose rejects 1-byte types.
fix: k_prior_bf16 = k_prior.view(nl.bfloat16); ... later moving = k_sb.view(fp8).reshape(..., 2).permute(...) to un-interleave parity
check_sketch: nc_transpose on fp8 tensor

rule: Mark unused block-table slots with -1 (int32) and load with oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip so the DMA skips them; keep a separate uint32 copy for dma_transpose which cannot skip.
why: Avoids reading inactive cache blocks (wasted bandwidth); the attention mask zeroes their contribution.
fix: INACTIVE_BLOCK_IDX = np.int32(-1); nisa.dma_copy(dst, src.ap(..., vector_offset=active_blocks_sb, indirect_dim=0), oob_mode=nisa.oob_mode.skip)

rule: Batch multiple folds/batches of indirect gathers into one dma_transpose call, capped at 64 positions on trn3 (32 on trn2 where TDG is unavailable); V batched dma_copy must pre-rearrange its index table to column-major order.
why: Reduces DMA instruction count; each DGE descriptor-generation call has fixed cost.
fix: cap = 64 if gen4 else 32; n_folds, n_batches = _compute_dma_batch_params(num_folds, bs, block_len, cap)

rule: Keep paged-KV block_len >= 8 after resizing; warn/avoid configurations that force block_len < 8.
why: Each block is one DMA burst; short bursts under-utilise HBM bandwidth.
trigger: resize_cache_block_len_for_attention_tkg_kernel reduces block_len to satisfy p_max multiples.
fix: if reduced_blk_len < 8: increase curr_sprior to a multiple of block_len*lnc*128

rule: Evict MM1 score groups from PSUM with predicated/strided tensor_copy that applies the mask and writes batch-interleaved SBUF columns, rather than copying then masking.
why: tensor_copy_predicated fuses the mask into the eviction; strided writes let several batches share one PSUM bank schedule.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy_predicated(src=qk_psum[0:128, 0:n*s_qh], dst=qk_sb_view[:, start:end:2], predicate=mask_view[:, start:end:2])

rule: Do not rely on the experimental QK-swap (Q-stationary, column-tiled) MM1 path; it is hard-gated off (`return False`) due to OOB errors, and only applied to block KV with curr_sprior >= 1024 and 4 < s_active_qh <= 128.
why: Production kernels keep K stationary; the swap variant is still being validated.
trigger: Considering Q-stationary scores for batch>1 decode.
fix: is_qk_swapped(...) -> False; keep K stationary

rule: Put the query heads that share a KV head side-by-side on the free axis of the Q moving tile so each K/V tile is loaded once per group.
why: Decode is bound by KV reads; grouping amortises each K/V DMA over `group` query heads.
fix: q_group = q[:, kv*group:(kv+1)*group]  # [d, group]; qk = nc_matmul(stationary=q_group, moving=k_tile) or vice versa
check_sketch: K/V loaded per query head

rule: To apply a per-column scalar (1/sum) that lives on partitions, transpose the column with 32-row vector-engine nc_transpose chunks into partition 0 and broadcast with nc_stream_shuffle, or use a single PE matmul with a stride-0 access pattern against an identity.
why: VectorE transposes are slower but VectorE is idle while PE is busy; the stride-0 AP trick does transpose+broadcast in one matmul.
trigger: Normalising [d, bqs] attention output by the [bqs,1] softmax sum.

rule: Broadcast a [1, F] row (e.g. gamma) across all partitions with nc_matmul(stationary=ones[1,128], moving=row[1, F]) into PSUM and consume directly from PSUM in the next op.
why: The PE performs a 1-deep contraction that replicates the row to 128 partitions, avoiding a 128-way DMA broadcast.
trigger: Per-feature scale vectors applied to [tokens, H] tiles.
fix: nisa.nc_matmul(dst=g_psum[0:P, 0:F], stationary=ones_vec[0:1, 0:P], moving=gamma_sb[0:1, off:off+F]); nisa.scalar_tensor_tensor(dst=x, data=x, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=inv_rms[:,0:1], op1=nl.multiply, operand1=g_psum[0:P,0:F])

rule: Reduce across the partition axis with nc_matmul(stationary=ones[128,128], moving=x[128, T]); accumulate several free-dim tiles into the same PSUM and leave the accumulate flag unset consistently.
why: VectorE/ScalarE cannot reduce across partitions; the PE does it as a rank-1 contraction. Mixing explicit and implicit accumulate flags into one PSUM is rejected (NCC_ILMM003).
trigger: RMSNorm sum of squares when H sits on partitions.
fix: psum = nl.ndarray((128, T), fp32, buffer=nl.psum); for i_d: nisa.nc_matmul(psum, stationary=ones_sb, moving=x_sq[:, i_d*T:(i_d+1)*T])
check_sketch: mixed accumulate=True/False on same PSUM dst

rule: Copy every matmul/transpose result from PSUM to SBUF as soon as it is complete; never feed PSUM as a matmul stationary operand (gen3+ disallows it) and treat PSUM as a scarce 8x2KB scratch.
why: PSUM is tiny; holding results blocks the next matmul group. nl.matmul(transpose_x=False) internally transposes into PSUM which cannot be stationary on gen3+.
fix: qk_sbuf = nl.ndarray(qk_psum.shape, dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.tensor_copy(qk_sbuf, qk_psum)  # or activation(copy)/tensor_scalar_reduce
check_sketch: PSUM tensor used as nc_matmul stationary; PSUM live across >1 matmul group

rule: Evict a PSUM score tile through nisa.tensor_scalar_reduce (VectorE) that scales and simultaneously produces the row max, freeing the PSUM bank earlier so the next QK matmul can start.
why: Frees TensorE sooner at a small VectorE cost; sets up software pipelining with fixed PSUM banks.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar_reduce(dst=qk_sb[:, i, :], data=qk_psum_bank, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=scale, reduce_op=nl.maximum, reduce_res=row_max_kv[:, i:i+1])

rule: With manual PSUM allocation, cycle QK score tiles through banks 0-6 and reserve bank 7 for the PV accumulation so the two matmul streams never contend.
why: Keeps the long-lived PV accumulator from being evicted by the rotating QK tiles.
fix: qk_psum = psum.create_ndarray(0, (128, 7*512)); attn_out_psum = psum.create_ndarray(7, (128,128)); bank = i_tile_kv % 7

rule: If NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE=true, restrict manual PSUM allocation to banks 0-6: the compiler lowers dma_transpose to an identity matmul that uses bank 7 as scratch.
why: Otherwise the kernel's bank-7 accumulator is clobbered.
trigger: Manual PSUM addressing with that env var set.
fix: num_banks = 7 if os.environ.get('NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE','').lower()=='true' else 8

rule: Address PSUM tiles manually with address=(0, bank_idx * 2048) and shape (128, 512) fp32; skip the address when the SbufManager is in auto-alloc mode.
why: One bank = 512 fp32 per partition; aligning tiles to bank boundaries avoids accidental bank sharing between accumulators.
fix: nl.ndarray((128, 512), dtype=nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum, address=None if sbm.is_auto_alloc() else (0, psum_idx * 512 * 4))

rule: Allocate a new PSUM ndarray per loop iteration for non-accumulating results (instead of reusing one) so the compiler can rotate banks and avoid accidental accumulation.
why: A reused PSUM destination implies accumulation and a WAW chain that blocks overlap.
trigger: Unrolled Python loops producing independent matmul outputs.
fix: qk_tiles = [nl.ndarray((128,512), fp32, buffer=nl.psum) for _ in range(n)]

rule: Accumulate the K-tiles of one block directly in PSUM (repeated nc_matmul into the same dst) and only cross K-blocks add into an SBUF result tile (tensor_tensor add) or nl.loop_reduce.
why: PSUM accumulation is free; SBUF accumulation costs a VectorE pass per block, so maximise TILES_IN_BLOCK_K (8 tiles = 1024 K) per PSUM round.
fix: for bk in range(8): nisa.nc_matmul(dst=res_psum, stationary=lhsT[bk], moving=rhs[bk]); nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=acc_sb, data1=acc_sb, data2=res_psum, op=nl.add)

rule: Order matmul loops N-block > M-block > K-block so the output block stays resident in SBUF and is stored to HBM exactly once.
why: Output is never spilled/reloaded regardless of K; only inputs stream.
fix: for n2: for m2: Z_SBUF = zeros((TILES_M, 128, TILES_N*512)); for k2: ... ; store Z_SBUF once

rule: Issue each HBM<->SBUF DMA as [128 partitions, (tiles_in_block * tile) free] rather than per 128x128 tile; coalescing is only possible along the free axis because K is split over partitions.
why: Larger contiguous bursts per partition raise DMA efficiency; the partition stride is fixed.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=rhs_tile[0:128, 0:BLOCK_N], src=rhs[k*128:(k+1)*128, n*BLOCK_N:(n+1)*BLOCK_N])  # BLOCK_N=1024+; pack result tiles into [128, BLOCK_N] before store
check_sketch: dma_copy with free size < 512 inside hot loop

rule: Use nl.sequential_range for the outer K-block loop that accumulates into SBUF so the compiler does not vectorise/reorder the accumulation.
why: Reordering would break the ordered SBUF accumulate chain.
fix: for k in nl.sequential_range(NUM_BLOCK_K): ...

rule: Allocate new SBUF input tiles for each K step instead of reusing one buffer so the next step's DMA can overlap the current nc_matmul.
why: Reusing one buffer creates a write-after-write dependency that serialises the DMAs behind the matmul.
trigger: K-loop with explicit dma_copy per tile.
fix: for kt in nl.affine_range(K_TILES): input_tile = nl.ndarray((128, M)); nisa.dma_transpose(dst=input_tile, src=buf[:, k_slice]); nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=input_tile, moving=weight_tile)
check_sketch: same SBUF tile written by dma_copy in every iteration of a loop containing nc_matmul

rule: Align SBUF buffers that are destinations/sources of dma_transpose to 32 bytes; manual allocators default to 32-byte alignment.
why: DMA transposes require 32-byte aligned per-partition addresses.
fix: self.offset = (self.offset + size + 31) & ~31
check_sketch: address % 32 != 0 for dma_transpose operand

rule: Replace nc_transpose+tensor_copy of the bf16 exp tile with nisa.dma_transpose(axes=(1,0)) straight into the [kv, q] SBUF layout when TensorE is the bottleneck.
why: Offloads the transpose to the DMA queues, leaving the PE for the matmuls.
fix: nisa.dma_transpose(dst=scores_t[:, i, :], src=exp_row[:, i*128:(i+1)*128], axes=(1, 0))
check_sketch: TensorE utilisation high with many nc_transpose

rule: dma_transpose does not support dynamic (indirect) access patterns (NKI-415); for indirect sources use dma_copy with a transposing .ap() into SBUF then nc_transpose.
why: Compiler limitation on dynamic offsets in the transpose DGE.
trigger: Loading bias/scale rows selected by a runtime index into a transposed tile.
fix: if src.is_indirect(): nisa.dma_copy(src=view, dst=tmp.ap(pattern=[[tile, n],[1, tile]]), dge_mode=0); nisa.nc_transpose(psum, tmp); tensor_copy(dst, psum) else: nisa.dma_transpose(src=view4d, dst=dst4d, dge_mode=3)
check_sketch: dma_transpose with is_indirect() src

rule: Expand dma_transpose source/destination views to 4 dims (expand_dim) before calling it; indirect dma_transpose also requires a 4-d source tile.
why: API constraint of the transposing DGE path.
fix: while src.ndim < 4: src = src.expand_dim(1); nisa.dma_transpose(src=src, dst=dst.expand_dim(1).expand_dim(1))

rule: Use static DMA (dge_mode=3 / _DGE_MODE_NONE) for weight and activation loads with compile-time offsets; let the compiler decide (dge_mode=0) only for indirect tensors; hwdge for ring-buffered weight slabs.
why: Experiments in the MLP TKG kernels show static DMA outperforms DGE for these loads; DGE is only needed for dynamic offsets (fallback if HBM OOM).
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=w_tile, src=w_view, dge_mode=3)  # or dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge; adaptive: 0 if tensor.is_indirect() else 3

rule: Fuse the residual add into the HBM load with nisa.dma_compute(srcs=[x, residual], reduce_op=nl.add) so it costs no Vector/Scalar/PE cycles.
why: The DMA engine can add two sources while moving data; the compute engines stay free for the norm/quantize.
trigger: Pre-norm residual add in decoder layers.
fix: nisa.dma_compute(dst=hidden_out, srcs=[x_view, add_view], scales=[1.0,1.0], reduce_op=nl.add); if sharded: nisa.core_barrier(hidden_out, cores=[0,1])
check_sketch: tensor_tensor(add) immediately after two dma_copy of the same shape

rule: Insert nisa.core_barrier(tensor, cores=[0,1]) after each core writes its shard of a shared HBM tensor that the other core will read next.
why: Without the barrier the consumer core can read stale HBM data.
trigger: LNC=2 dma_compute into shared_hbm followed by normalisation.
fix: if num_shards > 1: nisa.core_barrier(fused_output, cores=[0, 1])
check_sketch: shared_hbm written by shard then read by all without barrier

rule: Chain decode kernels with the transposed [H0, n_prgs, H1_shard, T] HBM layout (transposed_in/transposed_out) so each core does one contiguous DMA of its H shard with no on-chip transpose.
why: Avoids the [T,H]<->[H0,H1,T] relayout on every kernel boundary; the per-NC slab is contiguous.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=out.reshape((H0, nshard*nc_size))[:, shard*nc_size:(shard+1)*nc_size], src=down_sb.reshape((H0, nc_size)))

rule: Convert [H0, H1, T] output to [T, H] with per-token SBUF copies alternating ScalarE/VectorE into [H0, T, H1], then one dma_copy whose destination access pattern performs the transpose, instead of H1 PE transposes.
why: Removes PE/PSUM traffic from the output path and balances the copies across two engines; the DMA handles the final partition->row scatter.
trigger: Final store of a decode projection.
fix: for t: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=resh.ap([[T*H1,H0],[1,H1]], offset=t*H1), src=tmp.ap([[T*H1,H0],[T,H1]], offset=t), engine=scalar if t%2==0 else vector); nisa.dma_copy(dst=out.ap([[H1,H0],[H,T],[1,H1]], offset=...), src=resh.ap([[T*H1,H0],[H1,T],[1,H1]]))

rule: Alternate PSUM->SBUF evictions between ScalarE (activation copy, index even) and VectorE (tensor_copy/tensor_scalar, index odd); fold per-partition scale/bias into the eviction, but route full-shape scale/bias to VectorE tensor_tensor.
why: Two engines drain PSUM in parallel; ScalarE only accepts (P,1) operands for scale/bias.
trigger: Every matmul result eviction in decode kernels.
fix: interleave_copy(dst=out_tile, src=psum[...], scale=dequant[:,0:1], index=i)  # even->nisa.activation(copy), odd->tensor_scalar/tensor_tensor
check_sketch: all PSUM evictions in a loop on one engine

rule: A tensor_scalar with two multiply ops (op0=multiply, op1=multiply) can only run on VectorE (NCC_IBIR444); fold one factor into a tiny [P,1] operand so the wide op is a single multiply that ScalarE can also execute.
why: Keeps the ability to schedule the wide op on the less-loaded engine.
fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=recip, data=recip, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=scale_const)  # [P,1]; then nisa.tensor_scalar(dst=x, data=x, op0=nl.multiply, operand0=recip, engine=nisa.scalar_engine)
check_sketch: tensor_scalar(op0=multiply, op1=multiply, engine=scalar)

rule: Cast integer index tensors to fp32 before using them as tensor_scalar operands.
why: tensor_scalar requires fp32 operands.
trigger: Top-k / one-hot masks from int indices.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=idx_fp32, src=idx_i32); nisa.tensor_scalar(dst, idx_fp32, op0=nl.equal, operand0=k, op1=nl.multiply, operand1=w)

rule: Pick the engine for PSUM->SBUF spills by which engine is the kernel bottleneck at that point (e.g. ScalarE once the norm is finished, keeping VectorE free for quantize_mx).
why: Engine choice of copies is free; placing them on the idle engine shortens the critical path.
trigger: Any copy near a saturated engine.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst, src=psum, engine=nisa.scalar_engine)
check_sketch: copies default to the same engine as the bottleneck op

rule: Manage SBUF with a stack/heap allocator: open_scope(interleave_degree=N) + increment_section() for N-way multi-buffering inside loops, alloc_heap for buffers that outlive scopes, and track min_independent_addr so sub-scope allocations in section i do not alias section i+1.
why: Explicit addresses give the compiler no freedom to serialise; the section logic prevents the classic anti-dependency where a nested scope's buffer overlaps the next iteration's top-level buffer.
fix: sbm = SbufManager(0, 200*1024, logger); sbm.open_scope(interleave_degree=2); for i: t = sbm.alloc_stack(shape, dtype); ...; sbm.increment_section(); sbm.close_scope()

rule: Set a loop's multi-buffer degree to min(cap, free_sbuf_bytes // per_iteration_bytes) computed at trace time, after invariants are allocated.
why: Maximises cross-iteration overlap without overflowing the fixed SBUF region.
trigger: Token-tile loops in norm/quantize kernels; batch loops in attention.
fix: tile_interleave = max(1, min(_MAX_TILE_INTERLEAVE, sbm.get_free_space() // per_tile_bytes)); sbm.open_scope(interleave_degree=tile_interleave)

rule: Align small per-partition vectors (ones, eps, fp32 stats) to 4 bytes (align=4) when manually allocating.
why: Unaligned 4-byte vectors adjacent to 2-byte buffers caused a race (NKILIB-876).
trigger: Manual SBUF allocation of (P,1) fp32 tensors.
fix: bufs.one_vec = sbm.alloc_stack((128, 1), dtype=io_type, align=4)
check_sketch: fp32 alloc_stack without align

rule: Keep a memset-zero [P,1] fp32 bias tensor and pass it to nisa.activation calls that need a scale but no bias.
why: Workaround for a runtime issue when activation is given a scale without a bias vector.
fix: zero_bias = nl.ndarray((128,1), fp32); zero_bias[...] = 0.0; nisa.activation(np.copy, x, scale=s, bias=zero_bias)

rule: Structure attention as stage functions (qk_max, exp_sum, transpose, pv, write_back) and call them with skewed indices (i, i-1, i-2) inside nl.no_reorder(), double-buffering the SBUF/PSUM tiles the skew keeps live.
why: Lets TensorE (qk of tile i), ScalarE (exp of i-1) and TensorE/VectorE (pv/writeback of i-2) overlap; manual allocation plus no_reorder stops the scheduler from undoing it.
trigger: Compute-bound prefill attention; any multi-engine loop.
fix:
with nl.no_reorder():
  for i in range(n+2): exp_row_sum(i-1); qk_max_2xbuf(i); pv_matmul(i-2); transpose_scores(i-1); write_back(i-2)

rule: Index double-buffered SBUF state with (iteration % 2) along a leading free dim ([P, 2, ...]) so the producer of tile i+1 never overwrites what the consumer of tile i still reads.
why: Allows the skewed stages to run concurrently.
fix: bufs.qk_sbuf = sb.create_ndarray((128, 2, n_kv, 512)); idx = i_tile_q % 2

rule: Use nl.affine_range for independent iterations, nl.sequential_range only when an iteration reads state written by the previous one, and nl.static_range (Python unroll) when the body needs compile-time index arithmetic (edge handling) or when sequential_range mis-schedules.
why: affine_range gives the scheduler freedom (pipelining); sequential_range forces order; static_range unrolls and allows Python-level branching per iteration.
fix: # mamba_v3: 'FIXME: sequential_range gives incorrect answer and also much worse perf than static_range' -> for i in nl.static_range(n_seq_len_tile)
check_sketch: loop-carried SBUF dependency inside affine_range

rule: Load tensors reused across an inner loop (delta/u across states, K/V across query tiles) once in the outer scope.
why: Removes redundant HBM traffic; mamba_v2 vs v1 is exactly this change.
fix: delta_i = load once per channel tile; for i_state in affine_range(S): reuse delta_i
check_sketch: dma_copy inside inner loop whose src does not depend on inner index

rule: Chunk long free-dim elementwise/scan chains into ~512-element tiles so successive instructions pipeline.
why: Empirically profiled 'magic number' in the Mamba tutorial; keeps instruction size large enough to amortise overhead while allowing overlap.
fix: seq_len_fsize = 512; for t in nl.static_range(seq_len // 512): ...

rule: Express first-order linear recurrences with nisa.tensor_tensor_scan(op0=multiply, op1=add, initial=carry) and carry the last column into the next chunk's initial.
why: A native scan instruction replaces a serial loop over positions.
trigger: SSM / cumulative products along the free axis.
fix: nisa.tensor_tensor_scan(dst=res, data0=A, data1=Bu, initial=scan_init, op0=nl.multiply, op1=nl.add); nisa.tensor_copy(scan_init, res[:, -1:])

rule: Fuse a per-partition multiply into an activation via scale=[P,1] tensor (exp(delta*A) in one instruction).
why: activation applies scale before the function at no extra cost.
fix: nisa.activation(dst=deltaA, op=nl.exp, data=delta_i, scale=A_i)
check_sketch: tensor_scalar(multiply) immediately followed by activation

rule: Express bilinear/trilinear 2x upsampling as a few affine-index gathers over the loaded tile (nl.mgrid with i_dst = 2*i_y+1+i_x and i_src = i_y + i_x / i_y + (1-i_x)) combined in one weighted expression, with separate expressions for faces/edges/corners.
why: Affine index expressions over a SBUF tile lower to strided access patterns (no indirect DMA); each neighbour read is a strided view and the weighted sum is a handful of VectorE ops per chunk.
trigger: Upsampling / stencil ops where the compiler handles gather poorly.

rule: Chunk stencil/upsample inputs along the free (H or D) axis with a one-row overlap (step = chunk-1) and compute the shared boundary output rows from the chunk that owns both inputs.
why: Interpolation needs neighbours on both sides; overlapping windows keep every output computable from a single SBUF tile.
trigger: Any 1-neighbour stencil over a dim too large for SBUF.
fix: for h in nl.static_range(ceil((h_src-wdw)/(wdw-1))+1): start=max(0,h*(wdw-1)); end=min(wdw+h*(wdw-1), h_src); dst_start = 2*start+1 if start else 0

rule: When N*C (or H) is not a multiple of 128, use mask=(i_p < n) on load/compute/store with the full 128-partition mgrid instead of shrinking the tile.
why: Masking keeps instruction shapes uniform (no per-tail code) while skipping out-of-range partitions.
fix: in_tile = nl.load(src[i_p, ...], mask=(i_p < n*c)); nl.store(dst[i_p,...], value=out, mask=(i_p < n*c))
check_sketch: partition tile count not divisible by 128 without mask

rule: Implement pooling/windowed reductions as a strided .ap() view that exposes the window dims last, followed by one nl.sum/nl.max over those axes, not loop-based gathers.
why: A single instruction with a multi-dim access pattern replaces k*k shifted copies.
fix: pool_view = in_tile.ap([[H*W, P],[k*W, H//k],[k, W//k],[W, k],[1, k]]); nl.sum(pool_view, axis=[3,4])

rule: For free-dim gathers use data_tile.indirect(idx_tile, num_elem) where the index tile is laid out so that within every 16-partition group, output column i uses idx[start + (i % 16), i // 16]; build it by reshaping to (n/16, 16), nc_transpose (vector engine) and replicating with DMA.
why: The TI instruction reads the index tile column-by-column per 16-partition group; feeding it a plain row is silently wrong.
trigger: MoE routing gathers; any free-dim gather.
fix: reshaped=(n//16,16) via per-row dma_copy; nisa.nc_transpose(dst=(16,n//16), data=reshaped, engine=nisa.engine.vector); replicate per 16-part group; g = data.indirect(idx, num_elem=n); nisa.tensor_copy(res, g, engine=vector)
check_sketch: indirect() index tile shape != (P, n//16)

rule: Write new K/V rows into a flat cache with one indirect dma_copy whose destination uses .ap(pattern=[[1,B],[d,S],[1,d]], vector_offset=token_indices, indirect_dim=0); the DMA scales each index by the row stride.
why: One vectorised scatter replaces B scalar DMAs; the Vector DGE needs the source in SBUF.
fix: nisa.iota(batch_off, [[0,1]], offset=b0*S_max, channel_multiplier=S_max); token_idx += batch_off; nisa.dma_copy(dst=cache.reshape((B*S_max,d)).ap(pattern=[[1,B],[d,S],[1,d]], vector_offset=token_idx, indirect_dim=0), src=v_tile.ap(...), oob_mode=...)

rule: Select an output slot by a register-valued runtime index with .ap(pattern=..., scalar_offset=idx, indirect_dim=0); such values cannot be compared or used in Python control flow.
why: Runtime ids (e.g. collective rank) only exist as hardware registers.
trigger: Writing per-rank results, dynamic fold offsets.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(dst=out.ap(pattern=[[N,M],[1,N]], offset=0, scalar_offset=src_rank, indirect_dim=0), src=result_sbuf)

rule: Generate index/offset vectors on-chip with nisa.iota(pattern, offset, channel_multiplier) rather than loading them from HBM.
why: Cheap VectorE instruction; avoids a DMA and keeps indices in the right dtype (uint32 for DMA, fp32 for iota-based masks).
trigger: Batch offsets, parity masks, position-id masks.
fix: nisa.iota(ones_tile, [[0,1]], offset=1); even idx: odd partitions get 0xFFFFFFFF -> OOB skip
source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/experimental/transformer/attention_block_tkg.py ~2127, 2485-2493; attention_tkg.py ~522 (int32 for DMA, fp32 for iota)

rule: Keep two copies of a block index table: int32 with -1 sentinels for dma_copy(oob_mode.skip) and a uint32 cast (done once upfront on VectorE) for dma_transpose which requires uint32.
why: Different DMA paths accept different index dtypes; casting per fold in the hot loop is wasteful.
trigger: Paged attention K (transpose) and V (copy) loads.
fix: active_blocks_sb_u32 = cast once (int32(-1) -> float32(-1.0) -> uint32(0))

rule: Do not write an access pattern with two indices on the partition dimension (e.g. reshape_dim(0, [a,b])); linearise into one partition index and move the other factor to the free dim or a DMA offset.
why: The partition axis accepts a single affine index today.
trigger: Folding batch and block indices onto partitions.
fix: # 'Semantically correct, if two indices on partition were allowed' -> use scalar_offset DMA / flat partition index

rule: Partition offsets of tensor_copy operands must be multiples of 32 (quadrant); for unaligned cross-partition moves use nc_stream_shuffle with a 32-entry mask (255 = leave unchanged) through quadrant-sized temp buffers.
why: SBUF quadrants are the addressing unit for partition-offset copies.
trigger: Replicating Q into partition halves, packing small tensors.
fix: cross_partition_copy(src, dst, src_start, dst_start, n, free)  # tensor_copy if dst_start%32==0 else nc_stream_shuffle path
check_sketch: tensor_copy with partition start % 32 != 0

rule: Pass nl.NkiTensor slices (.slice/.select) rather than bare ndarray index slices into helper kernels that reshape internally; and stage data through a fresh contiguous buffer when an nc_matmul view fails BIR partition-step verification on a sliced buffer.
why: A bare slice loses parent strides and a reshape of a sliced view can violate partition-step checks.
trigger: RoPE_sbuf on a slice of cos/sin or of a larger Q/K buffer.
fix: tile_cos = sb_cos.slice(1, start, end); if enable_rope and not contiguous: out = sbm.alloc_stack((d,B,n,S)) and RoPE into it

rule: nc_transpose of 1-byte (fp8/uint8) data must write PSUM with element step 2; view the data as 2-byte or 4-byte packed types (fp32 holding 4 fp8) to transpose densely.
why: Hardware constraint on 1-byte PE transposes.
fix: quant_f32 = quant.view(nl.float32); nisa.nc_transpose(dst=psum[0:n,0:128], data=quant_f32[0:128, blk, 0:n])
check_sketch: nc_transpose on 1-byte dtype without packed view

rule: For nc_matmul_mx view data as *_x4 packed dtype (4 elems/word, K/4 partitions), place scales (uint8, P//8 rows) at offsets 0,32,64,96 of each 32-partition quadrant, and size quantize_mx outputs as (P, F//4).
why: Matmul-MX scaling groups are 8 partitions x 4 free; scales must sit in the quadrant their data came from; quantize_mx packs 4 elements per output element.
fix: scale_sbuf: for q in range(P//32): nisa.dma_copy(src=scale.ap([[F,4],[1,F]], offset=4*q*F), dst=scale_sbuf.ap([[F,4],[1,F]], offset=32*q*F)); nisa.nc_matmul_mx(dst, stationary, moving, stationary_scale, moving_scale)

rule: Build the MX interleaved SBUF layout ([P//4, F*4] gathering one element from each of 4 K-tiles) with a strided-read tensor_copy/dma_copy (.ap pattern) rather than a strided write.
why: Strided reads are faster than strided writes on both DMA and Vector/Scalar engines; the source can even be PSUM.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(src=sb.ap(pattern=[[4*F,P],[1,F],[F,4]]), dst=strided)  # or dma_copy from HBM reshape (4,P,F) with pattern [[F,P],[1,F],[P*F,4]]

rule: Resolve fp8 e4m3 to nl.float8_e4m3fn (max 448) on trn3/gen4 and nl.float8_e4m3 (max 240) on earlier generations; clamp quantization ranges accordingly.
why: The OCP variant only exists on gen4; the non-OCP range is 240.
fix: dtype = nl.float8_e4m3fn if nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen4 else nl.float8_e4m3

rule: In a ring all-gather+matmul, keep two private-HBM ping-pong buffers, issue collective_permute_implicit for the next step before the local matmul, and skip the final CPI.
why: Matmul and CPI both only read buf_cur, and CPI writes buf_next, so they run on disjoint engines; issuing CPI first hints the scheduler to overlap. Collectives cannot source IO tensors, so seed with dma_copy.
trigger: Tensor-parallel decode projections with ring overlap.
fix: nisa.dma_copy(buf0, input_shard); for step: if step < N-1: ncc.collective_permute_implicit(srcs_by_channel=[[buf_cur]], dsts_by_channel=[[buf_next]], replica_group=rg); matmul(buf_cur)

rule: Kernel return tensors must be nl.shared_hbm even when private HBM semantics are intended; the compiler disallows nl.hbm for returns.
why: Compiler restriction (noted as temporary).
fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm, name='out')

rule: Under LNC=2 split the KV-cache scatter by token range when BxS % 2 == 0 (both cores run identical K+V code), else put all V on core 0 and all K on core 1.
why: Symmetric op streams keep the cores in lockstep; the asymmetric fallback still halves the DMA count per core.
fix: batch_sharded = n_prgs > 1 and BxS % n_prgs == 0; do_v = batch_sharded or prg_id==0; do_k = batch_sharded or prg_id==1

rule: Ensure every kernel input is referenced on every core; an input consumed only on one LNC branch causes a compiler error (compute a dummy use on the other core).
why: The compiler rejects inputs that are dead on one program.
trigger: LNC-asymmetric code paths (e.g. token_indices used only for V on core 0).
fix: # K_cache_transposed and lnc=2: lnc=1 computes its own k_token_indices so token_indices stays used

rule: Broadcast a column src[:, j] onto all partitions of dst in one PE transpose by passing a free-dim broadcast view (.broadcast(1, B)) to nc_transpose.
why: Repeated input access on the PE replicates the column while transposing.
trigger: Per-token scalars needed on every partition.
fix: tp_psum = nl.ndarray((B, P), fp32, buffer=nl.psum, address=psum_address); nisa.nc_transpose(tp_psum, src.slice(1, j, j+1).broadcast(1, B)); nisa.tensor_copy(dst, tp_psum)

rule: Treat contributed kernels using `from neuronxcc import nki`, nl.load/nl.store, nl.par_dim, nki.compiler.sbuf.mod_alloc and @nki.baremetal(additional_compile_opt=...) as OLD API; with nki 0.6.0 use `import nki`, nisa.dma_copy, nl.ndarray(buffer=nl.sbuf, address=...), nisa.nc_matmul(dst, stationary, moving) and SbufManager-style manual addresses.
why: API renamed and allocation model changed; mod_alloc/num_free_tiles and --internal-skip-backend-allocation-opt-nki flags are not part of the new API.
fix: nl.load(x) -> t = nl.ndarray(x.shape, x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(dst=t, src=x); nl.loop_reduce -> explicit tensor_tensor add
check_sketch: import neuronxcc

rule: When hand-scheduling with manual SBUF/PSUM addresses (old API), decorate with @nki.compiler.skip_middle_end_transformations and pass --internal-skip-backend-allocation-opt-nki --disable-internal-io-dge; otherwise the compiler re-allocates and breaks the pipeline.
why: Middle-end transforms and backend allocation undo manual buffer placement; IO DGE adds descriptor overhead for static IO.
trigger: Fully manual kernels on internal builds.
fix:
@nki.compiler.skip_middle_end_transformations
@nki.baremetal(artifacts_dir='debug', additional_compile_opt='--internal-skip-backend-allocation-opt-nki --disable-internal-io-dge')

rule: Benchmark with nki.benchmark(warmup, iters, save_neff_name, save_trace_name) and read nc_latency percentiles; validate numerics first with nki.simulate_kernel on CPU.
why: Traces (.ntff) expose per-engine timelines needed to apply engine-balancing heuristics; the simulator catches layout bugs before hardware.
fix: bk = nki.benchmark(warmup=10, iters=100, save_neff_name='file.neff', save_trace_name='profile.ntff')(kernel); bk(x); bk.benchmark_result.nc_latency.get_latency_percentile(50)

rule: Group up to 8 PE transposes whose results can share one PSUM bank so the compiler can fuse them into a single 1024-wide PSUM write, and alternate the eviction engine per block.
why: Fewer PSUM allocations and larger evictions; explicit grouping is needed for the fusion.
fix: transpose_grp_size = min(8, block_len); for j in grp: nisa.nc_transpose(tp_psum, k_loaded[:, nl.ds(j*d, d)]); nisa.tensor_copy(k_sb[...], tp_psum, engine=vector if j%2==0 else scalar)

rule: For d_head > 128, dma_transpose each [s_prior_tile, 128] d-slice directly from HBM into k_sb instead of load + PE transpose + copy.
why: Frees TensorE for the matmuls and removes an SBUF round trip.
fix: nisa.dma_transpose(dst=k_sb_d_view, src=k_prior_view)  # per d_tile

rule: Load V tiles sequentially (contiguous rows) when strided_mm1 is set, otherwise as a strided horizontal tile; sequential gives better DMA throughput and the mm1 K layout is adjusted to match.
why: Contiguous bursts beat strided gathers; the strided_mm1 flag moves the stride cost to the (transposed) K load where it is cheaper.
fix: cfg.strided_mm1 = True  # 'Improves MM2 V read efficiency'

rule: Avoid implementing free-dim permutations as per-element nisa.tensor_copy loops (as in the transpose2d tutorial); use a strided .ap() view in a single tensor_copy or a dma_copy with transposing pattern.
why: The element-copy loop emits F1*F2 instructions; one AP-based copy does it in a single instruction.
trigger: Any [P, F1, F2] -> [P, F2, F1] swap.
fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=out, src=in_tile.ap([[F1*F2,P],[1,F2],[F2,F1]]))
check_sketch: tensor_copy with nl.ds(...,1) inside nested affine loops

rule: Keep QKV projection output, V, and attention output in SBUF across kernel boundaries when B*S fits one tile (n_bxs_tiles == 1); fall back to HBM only for large batch or MX paths.
why: Eliminates HBM round trips between fused decode stages; SBUF-resident inputs are supported only in TKG mode due to size.
fix: output_in_sbuf = n_bxs_tiles == 1 and not quant.is_mx(); params.input_in_sbuf / store_output_in_sbuf (TKG only)

rule: Choose the KV-cache update path by shape: block cache -> vectorised scatter; S_tkg==1 and B>1 (and not transposed K or B>16) -> batched vector DMA; else per-batch scalar DMA.
why: Vector DGE with indirect addressing amortises descriptor cost over the batch but is buggy for S_tkg>1.
fix: if is_block_kv: _update_block_cache(...) elif S_tkg==1 and B>1 and (not K_cache_transposed or B>16): _update_flat_cache_batched(...) else: _update_flat_cache(...)
